content.thinking:
I'm working through the causal chain for the postmortem, starting with the symptom: account page requests failing with error rates spiking after the feature flag was enabled, and I need to cite the specific error rate figures.

Tracing the "why" chain, the flag switch directed traffic down a new code path that raised a ZeroDivisionError at a specific line from a given timestamp onward, confirmed by the evaluation and flag-state data. I'm ruling out an unrelated feature flag change since it happened later than onset and couldn't have caused it, while confirming the fix (reverting just the monthly-spend flag) matches the recovery timeline even with that other flag still active. I'm also checking that no deploys occurred in the relevant window, since the rollout had already converged to a single revision beforehand, so deploys can be ruled out as a cause.

Then I'm tracing the actual mechanism: the average-spend calculation divides by the count of purchases this month, and for shoppers with zero purchases this month that count is zero, triggering the division error — a cause that rests on an unverified reading rather than something directly confirmed by the error trace itself.

This causes the account page request to fail. In plain terms: enabling the new feature routed account pages through a calculation that likely divides by this month's purchase count, breaking for shoppers who've bought before but not this month.

The division bug stays in the code even with the flag off, so re-enabling the monthly-spend feature without a fix would reproduce the same failure. As a contributing factor, there's no evidence of a test checking the monthly spend path for shoppers with zero purchases this month before the flag was turned on.

The existing test helper treats this as "the ordinary case" — if that assumption had been different, the division-by-zero would have been caught before reaching production. That's addressed by AI-2, the proposed fix that adds tests. A second factor is that the flag was flipped to full traffic almost instantly — going from 54/200 on to all 200 on within a minute — with no gradual rollout or error-triggered halt in place.

I'm also weighing whether the lack of paging matters: since Argus caught it anyway, a person being paged likely wouldn't have shortened the incident, so I'll fold that into the went_wrong section rather than treat it as a blocking factor. Moving on to look at the detection signals, starting with the account page error rate monitor.

For action items, I'm splitting the flag-rollout fix into two: a prevent item requiring feature flags for io-shop to be rolled out gradually in stages rather than all at once, and a detect item adding a check comparing account page error rate before/after each flag change that halts rollout if it worsens.

I'm also considering a process item requiring that flag-on paths be tested with shoppers who have past purchases but none this month before enabling in production, and an optional detect item linking the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so someone gets paged. For lessons, I'm noting what went well -- Argus correctly placed the onset and identified the flag -- and pulling the timing between alert and flag revert.

I'm also noting the draft PR #338 opened shortly after the alert, confirming the onset matches P1 exactly. On what went wrong: nobody was paged, and Investigator's ~32% estimate didn't match the measured figure. I'm also flagging that an admin flipped an unrelated flag during the incident before mitigation, which could have muddied attribution -- though it turned out to be a lucky break since that change didn't cause its own failure, as the service recovered once the monthly-spend flag alone was reverted.

Separately, I'm treating the second flag flip during an ongoing incident as a process failure worth calling out, and noting the assumptions underlying the figures -- that the error-rate series reflects account-page failures, that customer loss is estimated against prior weeks, and that pre-onset ClientDisconnected errors are background noise. I want to avoid citing specific numbers, though file paths like line references are fine since they're labels, not figures.

For the error rate description, I'll frame it as the share of HTTP requests answered with server errors. Drafting step one: shoppers' account page requests failed, with the error share rising from the baseline level before onset to the elevated average while broken, peaking at the worst observed value — citing AL1, Gbac1, and G5309. This confirms I've reached a cause.

action_items.item: Require a test of each new flag's on-path before the flag can be switched on in production. For this kind of feature, that includes a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
Switch feature flags on io-shop on in stages, for a small share of traffic first, rather than for all traffic at once.
Add a guard that compares io-shop's error rate before and after a flag change and stops the flag's rollout when the rate rises.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of all HTTP requests answered with a server error went from {series_before} before the onset to {series_while_broken} on average while the service was broken, peaking at {series_at_worst}. The service's own warnings about the account page error rate peaked at {Gbac1.7}.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors started at the onset and ran through the window that was read.

ruled_out.what: The other flag change, an-unrelated-feature, switched on at {P2.1}. It came after the onset, and the service recovered after only monthly-spend-feature was reverted, with that change still in place.
A deployment. No deploy came back for the day before the onset, and the only production change read for that day was the monthly-spend-feature toggle.

causal_chain.step: An admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. Before that, the flag evaluated off and account pages rendered normally. In the minute of {G971b.1}, {G971b.3} of {G971b.4} evaluations were already on. From then on, every evaluation was on. This sent account page requests down the monthly spend summary path.

Code-Fix read the source but did not run anything. By that reading, the monthly path, `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2}. That line matches the line in the logged error.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary sent account pages through a calculation that failed with a division by zero. It most likely failed for shoppers who have bought before but have not bought anything yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No test or check was seen that ran the monthly spend path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month before the flag could be switched on in production. By Code-Fix's reading, the existing test helper calls this shopper "the ordinary case".
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have shown up in testing, before the flag reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for all account page traffic within about a minute. No staged rollout was seen, and no guard was seen that would stop it as account page errors rose.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failing path, and the rollout could have been stopped before errors reached their peak.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

got_lucky: The second flag switched on during the incident did not add a failure of its own: the service recovered after only monthly-spend-feature was reverted. That kept the cause easy to pin to one change.
went_well: The Investigator placed the onset at the same minute the monthly-spend-feature toggle was recorded, and named that flag as the leading candidate.
Argus reverted monthly-spend-feature {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and judged the revert confirmed {T21.1 - T18.1} after making it.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, proposing a change to `average_spend_per_item_this_month` with new tests for review.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.
An admin switched on a second flag, an-unrelated-feature, at {P2.1}, while account pages were still failing. No hold on changes during the incident was seen.

input.root_cause: The code path that monthly-spend-feature turns on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of their purchases marked `in_current_month`. Nothing handles that number being zero. A shopper who has bought before but not this month therefore raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2}, and their account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The faulty division is still in the code behind the flag, so if monthly-spend-feature is switched on again before a fix is in, account pages would likely fail again for the same shoppers.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
